narrative:
Material PL2__M0D3D8F3 exhibits smooth demand behavior with a coefficient of variation of 0.43, 
indicating relatively stable and predictable consumption patterns. Historical demand analysis over 141 working days 
shows a mean daily consumption of 732 units with 96.5% active demand days. 
A statistically significant upward trend was detected (p=0.0075), suggesting growing consumption that should be 
monitored for capacity planning.

Lead time analysis reveals volatile variability (CV=0.63) with a mean of 2.24 days and 
standard deviation of 1.42 days. This volatility is primarily driven by transport factors, 
contributing 40% of lead time variance. The effective planning lead time of 3.67 days 
incorporates this variability to maintain the target 95% service level.

The optimized inventory policy recommends a safety stock of 1881 units (vs. SAP's 1960) and an 
order quantity of 12453 units, fully utilizing available storage capacity (100%). 
This configuration achieves a 45.7% cost reduction ($1134.48 annually) compared to the current SAP 
policy, primarily through reduced ordering frequency (15 vs 31 orders/year). 
The recommended reorder point of 4566 units provides adequate buffer against demand and lead time variability.
warnings: Safety lead time can be reduced from 3.0 to 2.6 days
Storage utilization >95% - capacity expansion planning recommended
Volatile lead times (CV=0.63) may impact service levels - consider supplier performance review
Significant demand trend detected - review forecast assumptions quarterly

research_insights.selected_model: Stochastic EOQ with Lead Time Variability
research_insights.selection_rationale:
Selected model accounts for both demand uncertainty (CV=0.43) and lead time volatility 
(CV_LT=0.63). The combined variance approach is appropriate for this smooth demand regime with volatile 
lead times. The normal demand distribution supports the use of normal approximation for safety stock calculation.
research_insights.boundary_risk:
Material operates at 100% storage capacity utilization, 
leaving minimal buffer for demand surges. The detected upward trend (slope=1.73 units/day) suggests capacity 
constraints may emerge within 6-12 months if growth continues. Lead time volatility (0.63) introduces 
service level risk that should be monitored through fill rate tracking.
